title: Make chat intent routing and execution outcomes deterministic
goal: Route incomplete create-file requests to a deterministic clarification before any provider or Skill execution, and expose explicit outcomes for clarification, denial, execution failure, and verified Skill success.
context: This follow-up broadens the narrow create-file regression into deterministic request preflight and an explicit execution outcome contract while keeping security and write verification unchanged.
forbidden_changes: Do not weaken workspace path allowlists, policy/approval gates, write size limits, or verification requirements.
Do not treat a provider-generated answer as proof that a tool action succeeded.
Do not modify release workflows or Alpha/Stable release configuration.
Do not claim physical-device verification without testing on a real iPhone.
acceptance_criteria: Incomplete create-file requests produce a deterministic clarification without invoking the provider, team orchestration, Skill execution, or workspace write module.
A request with a filename but no explicit content boundary asks for content or explicit confirmation of an empty file.
Complete create-file requests continue through the existing policy-gated and verified Skill route.
Execution outcomes distinguish needs_clarification, denied, execution_failed, and verified_success.
Regression tests cover Vietnamese/English incomplete requests, complete requests, no-write guarantees, and outcome status mapping.
All changes stay within allowed_paths and required CI checks pass.
The preflight grammar and built-in create-file Skill parser accept the same documented English command variants.
A filename without an allowed relative root/path is clarified before provider or Skill routing; runtime path policy remains authoritative.
verification: Inspect Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA workflow results.
On a physical iPhone, send 'hãy tạo file hello.txt' and verify a clarification is shown without a file write.
recovery: If contract validation or tests fail, fix the implementation or task scope; never bypass CI, weaken file-write verification, or mark device verification complete without evidence.
